title: MOSS: Multi-Modal Representation Learning on Sequential Circuits
problem: Circuit representation learning faces tradeoffs: LLMs understand RTL functionality but struggle with low-level netlist behavior; GNNs model netlists but fail on large sequential circuits due to long-range dependencies.
motivation: Accurate circuit representation is crucial for EDA tasks (placement, routing, timing prediction); sequential circuits pose scaling challenges for single-modality approaches.
method: MOSS fuses GNNs with LLMs: enhances D-type flip-flop (DFF) node features using fine-tuned LLM embeddings from RTL; GNN operates on reduced anchor points reducing long-range dependency burden; LLM provides global circuit embeddings for supervision; adaptive aggregation and two-phase propagation for signal modeling.
key_novelty: Multi-modal fusion of LLMs and GNNs, using LLM embeddings as critical node features and global supervision.
contributions: 95.2% accuracy in arrival time prediction for sequential circuits
Improved scalability to larger circuits vs. GNN-only or LLM-only
Two-phase propagation for sequential feedback modeling
baselines: LLM-only, GNN-only, existing circuit embedding methods
primary_theme: Multi-modal LLM-GNN fusion for circuit representation
